first.rationale: I currently intend to test simplified onboarding because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence suggests onboarding and signup friction affect early adoption and first-week activation. I will verify the two directly relevant records, plus promotional-pricing evidence to assess the competitor response tradeoff. A small guarded test protects against increasing low-quality signups or harming downstream qualified revenue while measuring activation, meaningful usage, retention, and qualified pipeline—not completion alone.

final.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding simplification experiment this week. The strongest directly relevant evidence shows shortened onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, addressing both current declines. Signup simplification also improved SMB activation and qualified revenue, though its slight retention decline warrants guardrails and segment-specific analysis. Do not use promotional pricing as the primary response: the verified discount increased qualified revenue short term but produced a 12% 30-day retention decline and failed the first renewal cycle. Evaluate completion, activation, time-to-value, qualified revenue, renewal retention, and cohort quality, with a rollback threshold for retention or renewal deterioration.
